A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mod-Adapter. Their complete text, equations, tables, rendered figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional material in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark comparisons, a user study, component and routing ablations, and generated-image examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative demonstrations of an extended model and additional concept combinations.

M1.justification: The main method is retained, but Appendix A adds an extension that concatenates reference-image VAE latents with noise latents, uses UnoPE to distinguish references, and applies LoRA to DiT joint attention. These additions substantially change conditioning and trainable components beyond v3's frozen-backbone adapter.

E1.justification: v3 trains only on single-concept examples. v4 adds multi-concept training using synthetic abstract/object combinations and MuSAR-Gen. Figures 10 and 12 also extend evaluation to four-to-five-concept compositions and weather/fog categories identified as unseen during training, substantially broadening compositional and generalization coverage.

E2.justification: Emu2, MIP-Adapter, MS-Diffusion, and TokenVerse remain the comparators in Tables 1–2 and Figure 3. The new appendix demonstrations introduce no additional evaluated comparator; MuSAR-Gen supplies training data and UnoPE is a method component.

E3.justification: Appendix A introduces an additional training configuration using 52,000 multi-concept samples and joint-attention LoRA adaptation. The retained benchmark construction, evaluation metrics, main 50K-plus-126K training schedule, and 32-participant user-study protocol are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that the main comparisons were rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 10–12 add qualitative case studies of four-to-five-concept customization, abstract/object recombination, and unseen-category generalization. Existing component, expert-count, clustering, and routing analyses are unchanged. No controlled ablation of the added extension is reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing averaging practices remain unchanged, and the added qualitative results introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical results, including Mod-Adapter's multi-concept CP·PF of 0.62 and single-concept CP·PF of 0.54. Figures 9–12 add qualitative outputs for additional compositions and generalization scenarios. Figure 10 concerns the adapted configuration, so it does not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including the modulation definitions, attention formulation, and pretraining loss, are unchanged. The appendix extension introduces no new formal derivations, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: tuning-free object and abstract-concept personalization, the Mod-Adapter components and VLM-guided pretraining, DreamBench-Abs, and superior reported performance. The appendix extension does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly attributes difficulty with many concepts to single-concept training and identifies loss of low-level details through CLIP image features, motivating the extension. The repeated-name and greater-than-three-concept limitations remain stated. Some existing ablation explanations also become more causally definite without new corresponding ablation results.

D1.justification: v4 adds extension data-construction details, a project-page pointer, and asset-license information in Table 5. It removes the code-release commitment and changes the hardware description from eight A800 GPUs to eight 80GB GPUs. Main hyperparameters remain unchanged; detailed extension budgets and LoRA hyperparameters are not supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations supporting MuSAR-Gen and UnoPE, plus GlassWizard and two deepfake-related works in the appendices. The main related-work discussion and positioning against TokenVerse and existing tuning-free personalization methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most scientific prose and the main section sequence are retained. v4 updates affiliations and publication headers, adds acknowledgments and Appendix H, expands the limitations discussion, and makes localized ablation explanations, heading-placement changes, and wording corrections.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the visual material with galleries covering abstract-concept examples, four-to-five-concept customization, recombination, and unseen-category generalization in Figures 9–12. It also redraws Figure 2, reformats Figure 4, and adds license Table 5. Existing quantitative table structures and earlier qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix A develops v3's brief many-concept limitation into an explained, illustrated extension, while the new figures broaden qualitative evidence. The gain is limited: the extension changes training data and several components together, lacks matched quantitative comparisons and isolating ablations, and is incompletely specified. The original quantitative evidence remains unchanged.
